mirabilia.page.greater_lens.1: The $(l:items/lens)$(item)Scrying Lens/$ lets me see a little more of the grid I draw upon. Ground from finer glass and bound in gold, a $(item)Greater Lens/$ widens my view of it far further: hexes much larger than before fit comfortably on the page.$(br2)It is worn and held just as the lesser lens is, and grants the same sight.
mirabilia.page.greater_lens.2: No craftsman's bench can make one. The glass must be reworked by $(l:patterns/great_spells/mirabilia_craft_greater_lens)$(action)a great spell/$. Like any lens it can then be $(l:patterns/great_spells/mirabilia_lens_imbuement)$(action)imbued with a hex/$, but only a Greater Lens takes $(thing)Deepsight/$, which lets that hex's writing show through walls.
mirabilia.page.entity_states.intro: A body's height and speed tell me only so much. These two patterns read how a creature is $(o)moving$(): whether it creeps low, or has just sprung from the ground.
mirabilia.page.entity_states.get_entity_: Transforms an entity into $(thing)True$() if it is sneaking or crouching, and $(thing)False$() otherwise.
Transforms an entity into $(thing)True$() if it is rising through the air under its own power, as in the first moments of a leap. Swimming, climbing, flying and floating do not count.
mirabilia.page.frost.intro: Cold is not a thing in itself, merely an absence of the restless motion that warms the world. With the right pattern I can ask a region to grow still.$(br2)Both spells below take a position and a radius of at most #{frost.maxRadius|block|blocks}. Their cost grows with the square of the radius: #{frost.baseCost} $(l:items/amethyst)$(item)Amethyst Dust/$, plus #{frost.perSquare} Dust per square block.
mirabilia.page.frost.freeze: Within the radius, still water turns to ice and every dry surface gathers a layer of snow. Casting again deepens the snow, up to a full block.
mirabilia.page.frost.thaw: The reverse of $(l:patterns/spells/mirabilia_frost#mirabilia:freeze)$(action)Freeze/$: within the radius, every snowdrift loses a layer and ice melts back into water. Every creature in it is warmed by #{thaw.frostSeconds|second|seconds} of frost, enough to stop a frozen one hurting, though powder snow soon takes it back.
mirabilia.mishap.bad_item.phial_room: a Phial with room for it (no Phial holds more than %s dust)
mirabilia.page.phials.blood_charge: Pours the given amount of a creature's health into the $(l:items/phials)$(item)Phial/$ in my other hand, at the same rate overcasting would take it. My own blood will serve, or that of any peaceful creature; nothing hostile will give up its blood this way, and another person's is not mine to take. It never leaves a creature with less than #{blood.floorHearts|heart|hearts}, so it cannot kill, nor takes more than the Phial has room for.$(br2)Villagers know when they are being bled, and do not forgive it quickly.
hexcasting.mishap.location_mirabilia.no_: there is no standing spell at %s
hexcasting.mishap.location_mirabilia.too: too many standing spells to raise another at %s
mirabilia.page.standing.intro: A hex ends the moment it is cast. A $(thing)standing spell/$ does not: it is a hex set to stand watch, running again and again on its own, paid for from a store of media I give it when I raise it.$(br2)While it stands it burns #{standing.upkeep} $(item)Amethyst Dust/$ every second, and #{standing.runs|time|times} each second it runs its hex, whose spells draw from the same store.
mirabilia.page.standing.rules: Each time it runs, its hex begins with its anchor on the stack: the centre of its block as a vector, or the entity it rides on. It reaches #{standing.range|block|blocks} around that anchor, and acts in my name only while it rides on me.$(br2)It ends when its store runs dry, when its hex mishaps, when it is dispelled, or when the entity it rides dies. It sleeps while its block or entity is out of the loaded world. I may keep #{standing.max} at once.
mirabilia.page.standing.raise: Binds a hex to the block at a position, with the given amount of $(item)Dust/$ as its store. Costs that much media, plus #{standing.startup} $(item)Amethyst Dust/$ to raise it.
mirabilia.page.standing.raise_entity: Like $(action)Raise Standing Spell/$, but the spell rides on the given entity, following wherever it goes. It may be any entity: myself, a creature, even a dropped item. If the entity dies or is destroyed, the spell goes with it.
mirabilia.page.standing.remaining: Given a position or an entity, returns how many seconds the standing spell there can last on its upkeep alone, or $(l:casting/influences)$(thing)Null/$ if there is none.
mirabilia.page.standing.feed: Pours the given amount of $(item)Dust/$ worth of my media into a standing spell's store.
mirabilia.page.standing.dispel: Ends a standing spell at once. Whatever media remained in its store is lost. Costs one $(item)Amethyst Dust/$.
item.mirabilia.greater_lens.imbued: Imbued with a hex of %s iotas
mirabilia.page.lens_imbuement.intro: Any lens, a plain $(l:items/lens)$(item)Scrying Lens/$ or a $(l:items/mirabilia_greater_lens)$(item)Greater Lens/$, can hold a hex of its own, and run it for me while I wear it, #{lens.runs|time|times} every second. Whatever the hex leaves on top of the stack, if it is a list of pairs, each pair a position or an entity followed by any iota, is written over my sight exactly where that place or creature is, following the creature as it moves.
mirabilia.page.lens_imbuement.cost: Each run takes #{lens.upkeep} $(item)Amethyst Dust/$, plus whatever the hex itself spends, from the lens's own store of media, never from me: it will never draw on my pockets or my health, and if the store is spent, its writing simply fades. $(l:patterns/great_spells/mirabilia_item_imbuement)$(action)Recharge Imbued Item/$ refills it. Its mishaps are gentle too, a note on my sight rather than a blow. Only I see what it shows.
mirabilia.page.lens_imbuement.imbue_lens: Stores a hex in the lens in my other hand, Scrying or Greater, and makes it a store of media from the given dropped stack of amethyst, consumed whole, as when crafting a $(item)Phial/$. An empty list clears it. Costs #{imbue.charged} $(item)Charged Amethyst/$.
mirabilia.page.lens_imbuement.example: For instance: gather every creature within thirty-two blocks of me, and turn each into a pair of itself and its name. Imbued with that, a lens names everything I can see around me.
mirabilia.lens.result.empty_stack: Lens: the hex left nothing on the stack
mirabilia.lens.result.not_a_list: Lens: expected a list of [position or entity, value] pairs on top, got %s
mirabilia.lens.result.no_pairs: Lens: nothing to show; the first item should be a [position or entity, value] pair, got %s
mirabilia.page.entity_states.get_entity_: Transforms an entity into its current health, two points to a heart. Things that have no health, like dropped items, become $(l:casting/influences)$(thing)Null/$.
Like $(action)Health Purification/$, but gives the most health the entity could have.
mirabilia.page.strings.intro: A $(thing)string/$ is plain written text, shown in gold upon my stack. Strings are how a hex speaks in words: the name of a creature, a number made readable, a message written on a sign.$(br2)Any of these may be laid over my sight through an imbued $(l:patterns/great_spells/mirabilia_lens_imbuement)$(item)Greater Lens/$.
mirabilia.page.strings.from: Turns any iota into a string, written the way I would see it on my stack.
mirabilia.page.strings.name: Transforms an entity into its name.
mirabilia.page.strings.split: Cuts a string apart wherever the second string appears, giving a list of the pieces. An empty second string cuts between every letter.
mirabilia.page.strings.parse: Reads a string as a number, or gives $(l:casting/influences)$(thing)Null/$ if it is not one.
mirabilia.page.strings.sign: Reads the writing on the front of the sign at a position, its lines joined by spaces, or gives $(l:casting/influences)$(thing)Null/$ if there is no sign. This is how I give a hex words of my own choosing.
mirabilia.page.strings.arithmetic: Strings answer to the same patterns that work on lists:$(li)$(l:patterns/math#hexcasting:add)$(action)Additive Distillation/$ joins two strings; if only one is a string, the other is written out first, so a name and a number join easily.$(li)$(action)Length Purification/$ counts the letters.$(li)$(action)Selection Distillation/$ picks one letter by its number, counting from zero.$(li)$(action)Selection Exaltation/$ keeps the letters between two numbers.$(li)$(action)Retrograde Purification/$ reverses it.$(li)$(action)Locator's Distillation/$ finds where one string appears in another, or -1.
mirabilia.page.names.intro: Beside the patterns that tell one kind of thing from another, a few more: whether a block is solid, what a thing is called, and whether two pieces of writing say the same.
mirabilia.page.names.block_name: Transforms a position into the name of the block there, as a string.
mirabilia.page.names.equals: Compares two strings and pushes whether they say the same, ignoring capital letters and any spaces at either end.
mirabilia.page.names.equals_strict: Like $(l:patterns/mirabilia_names#mirabilia:string/equals)$(action)Scholar's Distillation/$, but only true if the two are exactly alike, letter for letter.$(br2)For ordering, $(action)Maximus/$ and $(action)Minimus Distillation/$ and their second forms compare strings alphabetically.
mirabilia.page.names.get_block_solid: Transforms a position into $(thing)True/$ if the block there is solid, like stone, logs or glass, and $(thing)False/$ for air, water, grass, torches and the like.
mirabilia.page.craft_greater_lens.1: Reworks the $(l:items/lens)$(item)Scrying Lens/$ in my other hand into a $(l:items/mirabilia_greater_lens)$(item)Greater Lens/$. Costs #{greaterLens.charged} $(item)Charged Amethyst/$.
mirabilia.page.craft_greater_lens.2: The finer grind lets the eye take in a far wider stretch of the grid, and only such glass can learn to see through walls. Small wonder Nature guards the shape of this pattern.
mirabilia.page.join_phials.1: Grows the $(l:items/phials)$(item)Phial/$ in my other hand, where $(action)Recharge Item/$ would only refill it. Aimed at another dropped Phial, the two become one, keeping all the media of each. Aimed at a dropped stack of raw media, my Phial drinks in as much of the stack as it can at once, growing to fit.
mirabilia.page.join_phials.2: No Phial can grow past #{phial.max} $(item)Amethyst Dust/$. Costs #{joinPhials.charged} $(item)Charged Amethyst/$.
mirabilia.ward.owner_exempt.true: The stone will let your own hexes through
mirabilia.ward.owner_exempt.false: The stone will hold back your own hexes too
mirabilia.page.wards.1: Media flows where it is let. Marble from the dreaming world, threaded with charged amethyst, can be made to refuse it, and such a stone keeps a sphere of #{ward.radius|block|blocks} around itself out of every caster's reach: hexes of mine, of other casters, of circles and of stranger things alike.
mirabilia.page.wards.2: A $(item)Warding Stone/$ guards the places around it. Nothing within its sphere can be touched, sensed or targeted by a hex, wherever that hex is cast from.$(br2)A stone answers to whoever placed it: by default it lets its owner's hexes through. Touching it with an empty hand bids it to hold back the owner too, or to relent again.
mirabilia.page.wards.3: A $(item)Silence Stone/$ works the other way round. It guards nothing, but any hex cast within its sphere reaches nothing at all, not even its own caster. Patterns that only shuffle and reckon upon the stack still work; anything that would touch the world fails.$(br2)Glass from the dream's depths, around an echo of the deep dark, does the silencing.
mirabilia.page.ward_armor.1: Wards the piece of armor in my other hand. Costs #{wardArmor.charged} $(item)Charged Amethyst/$.
mirabilia.page.ward_armor.2: Whoever wears even one warded piece slips out of other casters' sight: their hexes can neither find nor target the wearer, though they can still strike at the ground beside them. The wearer's own hexes are unaffected.$(br2)Warding the same piece twice does nothing more, and the pattern refuses it.
mirabilia.dream.enter: You dream of glass under a turning sky
mirabilia.dream.wake.cold: The cold of the dream shakes you awake
mirabilia.dream.came_back_wrong: Something followed you out of the dream. Your hexes feel unsteady.
mirabilia.dream.no_beds: You cannot sleep inside a dream
mirabilia.page.tanakos_world.1: I have been there: a world of glass beneath a sky with no sun, where a vast wheel of stars turns forever. Sleep within #{dream.recordRadius|block|blocks} of an Akashic Record carries me back.$(br2)Its own spells are not written anywhere I know of in the waking world. Each must be found there, on scrolls the dream gives up, and until I have read one, its pattern means nothing.
mirabilia.page.tanakos_world.2: Each time I arrive somewhere new. The ground is glass, paler on the heights and darker in the depths; the old seabeds lie dry, floored in marble pebbles; columns of stone stand like the ribs of something sleeping. Fog hides all but the nearest of it. Whatever I carry comes back with me when I wake.
mirabilia.page.tanakos_world.3: Its heart is the one fixed thing: the galaxy's core hangs always above the north, while its three arms wheel slowly about it. A dreamer who keeps it in view need never lose their way.$(br2)Marble and the deep glass can be carried home, and both have their uses.
mirabilia.page.tanakos_world.4: Media will not answer in the dream. Every hex I cast there reaches nothing, as if I stood beside a $(l:items/mirabilia_wards)$(item)Silence Stone/$, and cyphers and trinkets refuse to stir at all. Nor can I sleep inside a dream.$(br2)And it is cold. The chill creeps in over #{dream.coldMinutes|minute|minutes}; leather keeps some of it out, a fire drives it back, and if it takes me entirely I am thrown out, hurt.
mirabilia.page.tanakos_world.5: To leave gently, I need only crouch and keep still for #{dream.stillSeconds|second|seconds} or so, and I wake in my bed (or wherever I last called home, if the bed is gone).$(br2)To die there is another matter. I come back with all I carried, but wrong: for #{dream.wrongMinutes|minute|minutes} afterwards #{dream.wrongPercent}%% of my hexes fall apart before they reach anything. Milk settles it, as it settles most things.
mirabilia.page.wake: Wakes me from the dream at once. It needs no media and no reach, which is exactly why it still works there. Cast while awake, it simply fails.
mirabilia.page.willing: Media is deaf in the dream, but the dream itself listens. A few patterns ask nothing of media at all: they simply $(o)want/$, and the glass and marble within #{will.reach|block|blocks} of me oblige. Wanting is tiring, though. Each of them chills me as much as #{will.coldSeconds|second|seconds} of the dream's cold. To tell them where, I use Dreamer's Gaze.
mirabilia.page.will_upward: The dream's ground at the given place, and in a small disc around it, rises by one block. Again and again, and I have a stair, a wall or a tower.
mirabilia.page.will_apart: The dream's ground around the given place parts, leaving a hollow three blocks across. Only glass, marble and pebbles answer; anything else stays where it is.
mirabilia.page.lost_dreamers: I am not the first to dream here. Villagers wander into this place too, and some never find the way out; what is left of them is drawn out thin, put back together wrongly, and flickers from place to place. They are drawn to the living, and the longer I linger, the more of them find me. Media draws them too: the more I carry into the dream, in amethyst, phials or charged trinkets, the sooner they come, and the sooner something worse comes with them.$(br2)Whatever cure works on the walking dead does nothing for them. They are too far gone.
mirabilia.page.dream_gaze: The silence hides even me from my own patterns: Mind's Reflection finds nobody, and Archer's Distillation sees nothing. But the dream knows where I am looking. This gives me the block I gaze upon, up to sixteen blocks away, or $(l:casting/influences)Null/$ if there is none; it works nowhere else.
hexcasting.mishap.bad_item.mirabilia.med: a dropped item or a container
mirabilia.page.wellsprings.1: A hex need not drink from my own pockets. I can point it at a $(o)wellspring/$, a store of media of my choosing, and for the rest of that hex every spell pays from the wellspring first. Only once it runs dry does the hex fall back on paying as it otherwise would: my inventory, a $(l:patterns/spells/mirabilia_standing)$(action)standing spell/$'s budget, a circle's impetus.
mirabilia.page.wellsprings.2: A wellspring can be a chest, barrel or other container full of amethyst; a stack of amethyst lying on the ground; or a minecart with a chest. (What I carry needs no binding: my hexes drink from it anyway.) Other people cannot be wellsprings. Their media is their own.$(br2)The binding lasts as long as the hex: one run of an imbued lens or a standing spell, one circle, one cypher. With a staff, it lasts until my stack is cleared and the spiral of patterns fades.
mirabilia.page.source.bind: Binds a container at the given place, or the given dropped stack or chest minecart, as the hex's wellspring. It must stay within reach: each time the hex needs media, a wellspring too far away (or warded) gives nothing, and the hex pays the usual way instead.
mirabilia.page.source.unbind: Releases the hex's wellspring; from here on it pays as usual.
mirabilia.page.source.media: Tells me how much media is left in the hex's wellspring, in dust, or gives $(l:casting/influences)Null/$ if none is bound.
mirabilia.page.lens_imbuement.sight: A lens only writes over what my own eyes can reach. It still remembers everything its hex found, but a place or creature hidden behind a wall goes unmarked until it comes into view again. Glass, leaves and the like hide nothing.$(br2)A $(item)Greater Lens/$ can be taught otherwise. Enchanted with $(thing)Deepsight/$, a rare gift of the dreaming world found only in its shrines, it writes through stone and earth alike, and shows me who waits behind the wall.
hexcasting.mishap.bad_item.mirabilia.len: a Scrying Lens or a Greater Lens
enchantment.mirabilia.deepsight.desc: Lets an imbued Greater Lens show its writing through walls.
hexcasting.mishap.mirabilia.not_dreaming: There was nothing to wake from
Only a dreamer's gaze is known to the dream, and I am awake
The waking world does not answer to will alone
mirabilia.page.tanakos_world.castles: Others have dreamed here before me, and some built. Here and there stand castles of white marble, walled, towered, with a tall keep at their heart: palaces of memory, raised by minds that are long gone. Some still stand whole; some have crumbled. Their keeps hold what their builders treasured, and the best of it is kept on the roof.
mirabilia.page.tanakos_world.listening_p: Far rarer is a thing I can barely describe: an egg of black stone a hundred paces across, half sunk in the land, glimmering with veins of light, open to the stars at its crown. Within, a vast circle is written into the floor in glowing glyphs, ringed with obelisks. I think it was built to $(o)listen/$.

At the circle's black heart rises a dais, and on it an Akashic Record among shelves: a library some earlier dreamer left behind. Six shelves still hold hexes, each under the key drawn on its spine; Akasha's Distillation reads them out. Every library keeps a different six: sights for a lens, wellsprings, dream-shaping, and old spells of the kind found in ancient cyphers. Chests around the dais hold the dream's best treasure.
mirabilia.page.dream_senses: The dream also lets me feel where I am, though no pattern of the waking world can find me there. $(action)Footing/$ gives the block I stand in; $(action)Bearing/$ the way I look, exactly, one block long. With these, a little arithmetic and $(action)Axis Purification/$ to keep my lines straight, I can will at places I am not looking at.
mirabilia.page.dream_footing: The block I stand in, as a position.
mirabilia.page.dream_bearing: The direction I am looking, one block long.
mirabilia.page.will_solid: A single block of dream glass forms at the given place, if it is empty. Small work: it chills me only a quarter as much as other willing.
mirabilia.page.snap_to_axis: Turns a vector into the axis it mostly points along, one block long, keeping its sign: a gaze a little off north becomes plain north. Where it is torn between the ground and the sky, the ground wins. Plain arithmetic, so it works awake or dreaming.
hexcasting.mishap.bad_item.mirabilia.imb: a tool or weapon that can wear out
an imbued lens, armor or tool
item.mirabilia.imbued: Imbued with a hex of %s iotas
mirabilia.page.item_imbuement.intro: What a lens can hold, so can the things I wear and wield. $(action)Imbue Armor/$ stores a hex in a piece of armor; while I wear it, it runs that hex for me #{armor.runs|time|times} every second, though it shows me nothing. $(action)Imbue Tool/$ stores one in a tool or weapon; it still works as it always did, but when I use it the hex is cast.
mirabilia.page.item_imbuement.media: Unlike a lens, these will not drink from my pockets. Each keeps its own store of media, made when it is imbued, and does nothing once that runs dry; though a hex inside may still bind a $(l:patterns/mirabilia_wellsprings)wellspring/$, which then pays first, as in any hex.$(br2)Bending a mere tool to magic takes its toll: every cast wears it, a point of durability and one more for every #{tool.dustPerWear} dust its hex spends, wherever the media comes from.
mirabilia.page.item_imbuement.imbue_armo: Stores a hex in the piece of armor in my other hand, and makes it a store of media out of the given dropped stack of amethyst, consumed whole, as when crafting a $(l:items/phials)$(item)Phial/$: the stack's media is both the store's size and its first filling. An empty list clears the armor. Costs #{imbue.charged} $(item)Charged Amethyst/$.
mirabilia.page.item_imbuement.imbue_tool: The same, for the tool or weapon in my other hand: its hex is cast whenever I use it.
mirabilia.page.item_imbuement.recharge: Refills the store of the imbued armor or tool in my other hand, up to the size it was made with. Given a dropped stack of amethyst, it uses only as much of the stack as it needs; given $(l:casting/influences)Null/$, it draws instead from my hex's $(l:patterns/mirabilia_wellsprings)wellspring/$. Costs one $(item)Amethyst Shard/$.
hexcasting.mishap.invalid_value.mirabili: a dropped stack of amethyst, or null with a wellspring bound
hexcasting.mishap.bad_item.mirabilia.tet: a lens, imbued armor or tool, cypher, trinket or artifact
hexcasting.mishap.invalid_value.mirabili: a vector, an entity or null
item.mirabilia.tethered.entity: Tethered to a moving wellspring (a dropped stack or minecart)
mirabilia.page.source.tether: Tethers the thing in my other hand that keeps a hex of its own (a lens, imbued armor or tool, a cypher, trinket or artifact) to a container, a dropped stack or a chest minecart. From then on its hexes drink from that wellspring first, whenever it is within their reach; out of reach, they pay as they always did. $(l:casting/influences)Null/$ cuts the tether.
item.mirabilia.media_sources_notes: On the Findings about Media Sources
item.mirabilia.media_sources_notes.desc: Some earlier dreamer's notes. Having read them, I can write what they taught into my own notebook.
advancements.mirabilia.media_sources.tit: On the Findings about Media Sources
advancements.mirabilia.media_sources.des: Find a dreamer's notes on wellsprings
mirabilia.dream.wake.mask: It wore you for a moment. You are thrown out of the dream
mirabilia.glass_man.holds: Something holds you in the dream
mirabilia.page.tanakos_world.glass_man: Linger too long and something comes for you: a man of glass, all but invisible when he stands still. He cannot be hurt. He walks a little faster than I walk and never loses me, and where he cannot follow he simply is somewhere else. A chime gives him away before he comes.$(br2)While he is near, the dream will not let me drift awake; only $(action)Wake/$ gets me out. His touch takes media, warmth and a little blood, and if I am already weak he wears me like a mask and throws me out, wrong.
mirabilia.page.tanakos_world.glass_man.2: If he is close when I wake, he comes with me, into the nearest villager whose mind was taken by Flay Mind, an empty shell he can fill. Such a villager stays his for good. He does no harm in the waking world; he trades. Each day he offers #{possessed.waresMin} to #{possessed.waresMax} foci with hexes already written in them, for $(item)Charged Amethyst/$.
mirabilia.page.ambient_media.1: Media spent is not wholly gone. #{ambient.castPercent}%% of whatever a hex costs lingers in the air where it was cast, and budding amethyst breathes out a little more as it grows. It fades slowly, halving in #{ambient.halfLifeMinutes|minute|minutes} or so, and seeps into the surrounding land.
mirabilia.page.ambient_media.2: Where much magic is worked, it gathers. Past a point the air crackles with sparks; past another it grows stuffy, and hexes cast there now and then fall apart before they reach anything. Past that, I am told, the dream itself comes close enough to touch.
mirabilia.page.ambient_media.reflection: Tells me how much media hangs in the air where I cast it, in dust.
mirabilia.dream.pulled: The air gives way, and you fall through
mirabilia.dream.pulled_along: Something drags you down with it
mirabilia.dream.thin_air: The air is thin here; something is very close
mirabilia.page.ambient_media.3: Where the air is thickest, a hex can tear it. Then the dream takes the caster, and everything living close beside them, and drinks half the media hanging there. The way back is the usual one.
mirabilia.machine.crystallizer: %s Amethyst Dust in, %s shards made; %s dust in collectors nearby
mirabilia.page.machines.1: Media that hangs in the air need not go to waste, and the Sun's own thinking can be caught. These devices do both. The two collectors hold what they gather, and a hex may bind either as a wellspring.
mirabilia.page.machines.discharger: It needs an upright lightning rod on top to throw from. When the media hanging in its chunk passes #{discharger.min} dust, it drinks #{discharger.percent}%% of it each second and throws it from the rod's tip as an arc into some living thing within #{discharger.range|block|blocks}, myself included; the more it drank, the harder it bites. Below that it rests, as does a redstone signal. Crude, but it clears stuffy air.
mirabilia.page.machines.ambient: A farmer's mind, steeped in growing things, flayed into budding amethyst. It draws #{collector.percent}%% of its chunk's ambient media each second and keeps up to #{collector.capacity} dust.
mirabilia.page.machines.solar: Its making needs the inscribed stone of the listening posts, whose sigils seem to drink the light. Under open sky in the overworld it catches #{solar.atNoon} dust each second at noon, less as the sun sinks, none at night, little in rain and almost nothing in a storm. It keeps up to #{solar.capacity} dust.
mirabilia.page.machines.crystallizer: Fed Amethyst Dust from above or the sides, it draws #{crystallizer.media} dust of media from collectors within #{crystallizer.range|block|blocks} and presses #{crystallizer.dust} dust into a shard every #{crystallizer.seconds|second|seconds}; shards come out below. It prefers sunlight when it can get it.
mirabilia.page.machines.read_the_sun: How strongly the Sun thinks where I stand, from 0 to 1. Nothing in other worlds.
advancements.mirabilia.listening_post.de: Find a listening post in Tanako's World
advancements.mirabilia.root.title: Thoughts of the Sun
advancements.mirabilia.root.description: Hold something of Mirabilia Hexica, or stand where the air sparks with media
advancements.mirabilia.high_voltage.desc: Be near when a Discharger's arc kills a creature
advancements.mirabilia.background_harves: Flay a farmer's mind into budding amethyst to make an Ambient Collector

hexcasting.mishap.mirabilia.macro.no_own: Only a person can keep macros
hexcasting.mishap.mirabilia.macro.full: I can hold no more than %s macros
mirabilia.page.macros.1: Some hexes I cast so often that drawing them out each time grows tiresome. A $(thing)macro/$ is a short pattern of my own choosing that stands for a whole hex: drawn in any hex I cast, it runs that hex in its place, just as $(l:patterns/meta#hexcasting:eval)$(action)Hermes' Gambit/$ would, at a cost of #{macros.callCost} $(item)Amethyst Dust/$ a call.
mirabilia.page.macros.2: Macros are mine alone: nobody else can call them, and a circle or a standing spell, cast by nobody, cannot either. A pattern that already means something, whether a pattern of the art, a great spell, a number or $(action)Bookkeeper's Gambit/$, cannot become a macro.$(br2)At first I can keep #{macros.start}. Milestones along the way (enlightenment, my first dream, finding a listening post, my first deal with the Glass Man) let me keep more, up to #{macros.max}.
mirabilia.page.macros.bind: Binds the pattern to the hex in the list as one of my macros; binding a macro again replaces its hex. The pattern must be given as an iota, so I write it after $(action)Consideration/$. Costs #{macros.bindCharged} $(item)Charged Amethyst/$.
mirabilia.page.macros.release: Forgets my macro for the given pattern, freeing its place.
mirabilia.page.macros.list: Pushes a list of the patterns of all my macros.
mirabilia.page.dreams_of_glass: Some of the old texts speak of a place reached only in sleep: a world of glass beneath a sky with no sun. I believe the $(item)Akashic Records/$ are a window onto it. If I sleep within #{dream.recordRadius|block|blocks} of one, I think I shall see it for myself.$(br2)What I learn there, I will write down properly once I have been.
mirabilia.page.machines.solar_plain: Under open sky in the overworld it catches #{solar.atNoon} dust each second at noon, less as the sun sinks, none at night, little in rain and almost nothing in a storm. Obsidian, cold and patient, holds what it catches. It keeps up to #{solar.capacity} dust.
hexcasting.mishap.mirabilia.no_mind: Only a person has words and memories to read
mirabilia.page.strings.chat: Something I said aloud, as a string: 0 is the last thing I said, 1 the one before, and so on, back through my last #{chat.history|message|messages}; $(l:casting/influences)$(thing)Null/$ past that. Only my own words: what others say never gets in the way.
mirabilia.page.strings.palace: The old orators kept their speeches in imagined buildings, a thought in every room. I can do as much: my $(thing)mind palace/$ has #{palace.rooms|room|rooms}, numbered from 0 to #{palace.lastRoom}, each able to hold a string. What I put there stays, through sleep, death and dreams, and is mine alone.
mirabilia.page.strings.memory_write: Puts the string into the given room of my mind palace, replacing whatever was there; $(l:casting/influences)$(thing)Null/$ empties the room. Costs #{palace.writeCost} $(item)Amethyst Dust/$.
mirabilia.page.strings.memory_read: What is kept in the given room of my mind palace, or $(l:casting/influences)$(thing)Null/$ if it stands empty.
mirabilia.page.strings.palace_size: How many rooms of my mind palace hold something.
